newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine sugar industry sees glut persisting.
newsitem.headline: Philippine sugar industry sees glut persisting.

text.p: A top Philippine sugar industry leader said on Tuesday he expected the domestic sugar glut to persist beyond the present crop year which ends on August 31.

Jose Maria Zabaleta, executive director of Philippine Sugar Millers Association, said domestic output during the present crop year will reach 1.86 million tonnes, translating to a supply surplus of 400,000 tonnes.
He said the surplus was caused by over-importation in recent months.
"I think it will be irresponsible to import unless it's the countertrade," Zabaleta told a forum on food and agribusiness.
He added that the surplus situation would not be corrected in the next crop year, predicting a surplus of 182,496 tonnes.

The Philippines is a beneficiary of a quota programme under which the United States buys sugar from developing countries at premium prices. In return, the state agency National Food Authority can import sugar from United States tariff-free.
Earlier, Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa said it would import 300,000 and 350,000 tonnes of sugar for the 1997/98 year since the glut would be wiped out by the end of August.
